nodes.description: Five homozygous missense alleles have been reported: R316Q, S319F, R322Q and H271P in the catalytic domain, and R96P in the substrate-recognition lid outside the catalytic site. Four of the five have been characterised biochemically and reduce or abolish FTO demethylase activity, so the characterised alleles converge on the same molecular consequence from two different parts of the protein. H271P has not been assayed for demethylase activity in the report describing it; the case for it rests on homozygosity in a consanguineous patient, absence from population databases, and its location in the catalytic domain.

evidence.snippet: Pregnancy was complicated by multiple fetal anomalies in diverse systems as follows: (1) uterine environmental (polyhydramnios, intrauterine growth restriction (estimated fetal weight <1%), umbilical cord thickening with increased volume of Wharton’s jelly, and elevated uterine artery Doppler indices with preserved diastolic flow); (2) central nervous system (CNS; poor gyral development, small cerebral hemispheres, and Dandy-Walker spectrum anomaly with incompletely rotated vermis, large foramen of Magendie, large cisterna magna, and hydrocephalus); (3) musculoskeletal (all long bones <5% mean for gestational age without evidence of fracture, thoracic cage 9% mean for gestational age, and disorganized anterior maxillary tooth buds); and (4) cardiovascular (ventricular septal defect, hypoplastic mitral valve, and aortic arch) (Table 1).

nodes.description: Loss of Fto shifts the balance between the two branches of Wnt signalling - canonical signalling falls because beta-catenin fails to translocate to the nucleus, while the non-canonical Wnt/calcium branch is activated through CaMKII and PKC-delta - and produces short, absent or disorganised cilia. In zebrafish this is accompanied by growth retardation, craniofacial dysmorphism, aberrant neural crest cell migration, microcephaly, situs inversus and renal cystogenesis, and Fto knockout mice show tissue-specific ciliary abnormality. This is the only worked-out route from FTO loss to a developmental phenotype, and it has been shown only in model systems: no patient tissue has been examined for either the Wnt shift or the ciliary defect.
